land.text: Kabul and Ghazni, 'A third son, Ulugh Beg II, became ruler of Kabul and Ghazni' (Abu Sa'id page); Cliopatria's outline of 1475 (116,849 km2, 64 cells)

predecessors.note: The Abu Sa'id page divides the empire's remains among his sons after his execution on 5 February 1469 and gives Kabul and Ghazni to Ulugh Beg II; the Ulugh Beg II page has him governing 'as an independent monarch' after his father's death. Cliopatria's Timurid Empire row loses this shape in 1475 and its own Kapisa row starts then; the dossier starts at the partition.

land.text: Kabul, taken by Babur in October 1504 ('Emir of Kabul' October 1504 - 21 April 1526)

successors.note: Babur held Kabul from October 1504 to 1526, when he founded the Mughal Empire. Cliopatria keeps its Kapisa row to 1506 and returns 401 of the 403 cells to its Timurid Empire row in 1507; the Babur page says nothing of Kabul in 1506 and gives Babur the city from October 1504, so the hand-over is dated to then.

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: The Babur page: Kabul 'was ruled by Babur's paternal uncle Ulugh Beg II', claimed by Mukim Beg Arghun, captured by Babur in October 1504. The Abu Sa'id page has Ulugh Beg II 'ruler of Kabul and Ghazni' from his father's death in 1469.

correction.text: Kabul and Ghazni, 'A third son, Ulugh Beg II, became ruler of Kabul and Ghazni': the 1475 shape unchanged, years extended back to the partition of Abu Sa'id's lands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Kapisa row begins in 1475 and draws 1469-74 inside its Timurid Empire shape. The Abu Sa'id page (executed 5 February 1469) gives Kabul and Ghazni to Ulugh Beg II in the division that followed, without a year for the division itself. Cliopatria's 1475 outline (67.5-71.7 E, 32.7-37.6 N) contains both cities and is used for 1469-74; no page gives a boundary.

116,849 km2 (67.5-71.7 E, 32.7-37.6 N) for 1475-1501: the Kabul principality, not the 'Kapisa' of the row's name. The Kapisa page is a disambiguation: the Kingdom of Kapisa belongs to 'the 1st millennium', the city of Kapisi lies 'near modern Bagram', and it has nothing for 1400-1520. The Abu Sa'id and Ulugh Beg II pages name Kabul and Ghazni ('given the cities of Kabul and Ghazni by his father'), both inside the outline; no page names another town or gives a boundary or an area (no infobox), so the extent beyond the two cities is Cliopatria's. The row is kept as a Timurid principality; the name is wrong.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid 1502 to October 1504: Babur captured Kabul in October 1504 and from then the land belongs to the timurid-empire dossier (Cliopatria keeps the Kapisa row to 1506)

keyframe_review.note: 116,849 km2, unchanged outline; the verdict changes the years only. Ulugh Beg II 'died in 1502 leaving only an infant as heir' (Abd ur-Razaq Mirza); Mukim Beg of the Arghun dynasty claimed the city (the Arghun dynasty page: 'In 1501/1502 Mukim had peacefully gained the submission of Kabul'); 'In October 1504, Babur was able to cross the snowy Hindu Kush mountains and capture Kabul'. The Babur page has nothing for Kabul in 1506 and does not mention Ghazni, so the shape's southern part after 1504 is unverified.

region.text: Kabul and Ghazni, 'A third son, Ulugh Beg II, became ruler of Kabul and Ghazni': Cliopatria's 1475 outline

ledger.note: 1469: Abu Sa'id is executed ('Yadgar Muhammad had Abu Sa'id executed on 5 February 1469') and 'What remained of the empire was divided among various princes': 'A third son, Ulugh Beg II, became ruler of Kabul and Ghazni.' The page gives the death date but no year for the division itself, so the year is the page's death year and the outline is Cliopatria's (confidence 2). The Ulugh Beg II page has him 'given the cities of Kabul and Ghazni by his father' (infobox reign 1461-1502) and governing 'as an independent monarch' after Abu Sa'id's death. Cliopatria starts this row in 1475; the timurid-empire dossier needs a matching 1469 loss of Kabul and Ghazni.

1501/1502: Ulugh Beg II dies and Mukim Arghun takes Kabul. The Arghun dynasty page: 'In 1501/1502 Mukim had peacefully gained the submission of Kabul, which was in chaos after the death of its ruler Ulugh Beg II.' The Babur page: Ulugh Beg II 'died in 1502 leaving only an infant as heir' and the city 'was then claimed by Mukim Beg of Arghun dynasty, who was considered to be a usurper' (undated); the Ulugh Beg II page says the same death year. The year 1502 is the death year on two pages; the Arghun page's 1501/1502 is why this is confidence 2. Same land, new ruling line (rule 2).

region.text: Kabul and its principality, captured by Babur in October 1504

ledger.note: October 1504: Babur takes Kabul and the principality ends. 'In October 1504, Babur was able to cross the snowy Hindu Kush mountains and capture Kabul' from 'the remaining Arghun chieftains, who were forced to retreat to Kandahar'; infobox 'Emir of Kabul', reign 'October 1504 - 21 April 1526', predecessor Mukim Beg. The Arghun dynasty page agrees: Babur 'besieged and took the city in 1504; Mukim fell back to Kandahar'. The land passes to the Timurid line (the timurid-empire dossier's October 1504 gain of Kabul). Cliopatria keeps its Kapisa row to 1506, but the Babur page has nothing for Kabul in 1506.

wars.name: Babur's conquest of Kabul
wars.outcome: Babur crossed the Hindu Kush in October 1504 and captured Kabul; the Arghun chieftains retreated to Kandahar, which Babur annexed from them in 1522.
wars.note: The Babur page gives no battle and no date for Mukim Beg's seizure of Kabul; the Arghun dynasty page dates it 1501/1502 and has Babur 'besieged and took the city in 1504'.

certainty.note: Mountain principality with no boundary on any page opened; the shape is Cliopatria's outline.

sources.title: Kapisa
sources.note: A disambiguation page: Kapisa Province, the Kingdom of Kapisa of the 1st millennium, the city of Kapisi near Bagram and the deity Hanuman. Nothing on 1400-1520.

sources.title: Babur
sources.note: Kabul under Ulugh Beg II to 1502, claimed by Mukim Beg Arghun, Babur in Kabul from October 1504 (Emir of Kabul 1504-1526, predecessor Mukim Beg), Kandahar 1522. Reopened 2026-10-19 after review: no Kabul event dated 1506; Ghazni not mentioned.

sources.title: Abu Sa'id Mirza
sources.note: Executed 5 February 1469; the remains of the empire divided among his sons, 'Ulugh Beg II, became ruler of Kabul and Ghazni'; no year for the division itself.

sources.title: Ulugh Beg II
sources.note: Reign 1461-1502 (infobox); 'given the cities of Kabul and Ghazni by his father'; governed 'as an independent monarch' after Abu Sa'id's death; died 1502; the infant Abdur Razaq usurped by a minister; Mukim took control of Kabul.

sources.title: Arghun dynasty
sources.note: 'In 1501/1502 Mukim had peacefully gained the submission of Kabul'; Babur 'besieged and took the city in 1504; Mukim fell back to Kandahar'.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Kapisa' is mislabelled: the Kapisa page is a disambiguation and its dated entry is the Kingdom of Kapisa 'in the 1st millennium'. The shape (1475-1506, 116,849 km2, Afghanistan and Pakistan, 67.5-71.7 E, 32.7-37.6 N) is the Timurid principality of Kabul and Ghazni under Ulugh Beg II (to 1502), the Arghun usurper Mukim Beg and, from October 1504, Babur. Repaired after review (2026-10-19): (1) the state now ends in October 1504, when the Babur page gives Babur Kabul ('Emir of Kabul', October 1504 - 21 April 1526); the 1505-06 years of Cliopatria's shape are not drawn here because the timurid-empire dossier already gains Kabul in October 1504; (2) the state now starts in 1469, the year of Abu Sa'id's execution and the division of his lands ('Ulugh Beg II, became ruler of Kabul and Ghazni'), not Cliopatria's 1475; 1469-74 is a new keyframe with Cliopatria's 1475 outline. Overlap with timurid-empire (decision of the author: keep this dossier, do not fold it; the colour agent seeded 'kapisa' and the validator needs every shape of the slug reviewed; the orchestrator may still fold both): the timurid-empire dossier adds admin1 Kabul to its own shape in its 1475, 1487 and 1497 corrections and records no loss of Kabul and Ghazni in 1469. For Kabul not to be drawn twice, its owner (ia-02) should drop admin1 Kabul (and Ghazni) from those corrections and from its 1468-74 shape, enter a loss to kapisa in 1469 (Abu Sa'id page), and change the counterpart of its October 1504 Kabul gain from 'Kabul (previous holder not named on the page)' to kapisa. Needs a dossier from another group: the Arghun dynasty of Kandahar (retreated there in 1504; Babur 'besieged and annexed Kandahar' in 1522; the Arghun page also has Mukim fighting Babur at Kandahar in 1507 or 1508; Cliopatria has no row). Not settled: the year of the partition (the Abu Sa'id page dates the death, 5 February 1469, not the division), Ulugh Beg II's own reign start (1461 in the Ulugh Beg II infobox, given the cities 'by his father', so before the state became independent), Mukim's seizure (Arghun page 1501/1502, Babur page undated), the shape's extent beyond Kabul and Ghazni (no page gives a boundary), and Ghazni after 1504 (the Babur page is silent). Pages: Kapisa, Babur, Abu Sa'id Mirza, Ulugh Beg II, Arghun dynasty (5 against a 1-2 page budget; the extra three were opened to repair the review's findings).
